attributes.translation: After (continuously) worrying about what to do after graduation, I decided to start a business.
attributes.nuance_translation: An expression highlighting that as a conclusion of (A), (B). On the tip of (A)'s completion (B). Regularly indicating effort to reach completion.

attributes.body_ja:
動詞（どうし）の過去形（かこけい）や「の」を伴（ともな）う名詞（めいし）と結（むす）びつく「末（すえ）」は、「先端（せんたん）」や「終（お）わり」を意味（いみ）する名詞（めいし）です。この後（うし）ろに「に」が付（つ）くと、その「先端（せんたん）」から何（なに）かの結果（けっか）が生（しょう）じることを表（あらわ）します。

この文法（ぶんぽう）はふつう「(A) の後（あと）に (B)」や「(A) の結果（けっか） (B)」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）しますが、ニュアンスとしては、その途中（とちゅう）でさまざまな出来事（できごと）が起（お）こり、最終的（さいしゅうてき）に (A) という「終点（しゅうてん）」や「結論（けつろん）」に至（いた）ったということを表（あらわ）します。

「末（すえ）」は肯定的（こうていてき）な結果（けっか）にも否定的（ひていてき）な結果（けっか）にも使（つか）われますが、どちらの場合（ばあい）も、長（なが）く続（つづ）いた努力（どりょく）や苦労（くろう）が最終的（さいしゅうてき）に (B) という結果（けっか）になった、ということが仄（ほの）めかされています。
attributes.body:
Appearing with verbs in their past form, or grouped with nouns after の is 末（すえ）, a word meaning 'end tip'. に will follow 末（すえ） , marking the 'tip' as the point from which something will result.

While this grammar pattern is usually translated as 'after (A), (B)', or 'as a result of (A), (B)', the nuance is on various things having happened along the way, and then finally reaching the 'point' or 'conclusion' of (A).

末（すえ）に may highlight either positive or negative results, but will suggest that some long-lasting effort or struggle eventually resulted in (B).

attributes.source: A Dictionary of Advanced Japanese Grammar
A Handbook of Japanese Grammar Patterns

attributes.body: Both た末・の末 and あげく convey the end of a process, but with subtle differences. た末・の末 often implies a significant sequence of events or actions over an extended period leading to the final result, as in 長い議論の末、結論に達した (After long discussion, we reached a conclusion). あげく, in contrast, is often used when the outcome is disappointing or problematic, as in 迷ったあげく、遅刻してしまった (After much hesitation, I ended up being late).

second_relatable.title: あげく
second_relatable.meaning: After, In the end, After all, Eventually

attributes.body: Both can express the idea of 'after doing (A), (B)', but 上で focuses on process or sequence (lit. 'upon' doing), e.g. 話し合った上で決めましょう ('Let's decide after discussing it.'). In contrast, た末・の末 emphasizes an outcome after prolonged effort or struggle, e.g. 悩んだ末に転職した ('After much deliberation, I changed jobs.').
